holidays.name: Harry Potter's Birthday
holidays.description: Fans around the world celebrate the birthday of the Boy Who Lived with themed parties, butterbeer, cake, movie marathons, and a lot of wand waving. It is also the birthday of author J.K. Rowling, so the day doubles as a celebration of the whole wizarding world.
holidays.origin: In the books, Harry James Potter is born on July 31, 1980. J.K. Rowling chose to share her own July 31 birthday with her hero, and fans have turned the date into an annual unofficial holiday.
holidays.funFact: J.K. Rowling was born on July 31, 1965, so she and Harry share a birthday exactly 15 years apart. Neville Longbottom also has a birthday on July 30, just one day earlier.

holidays.name: National Raspberry Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate sweet and tart raspberry cake, whether layered with raspberry filling, swirled into frosting, or baked with fresh berries. Bakers and dessert lovers are encouraged to treat themselves to a slice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of the American tradition of dedicated food days, which are popularized by food bloggers, bakeries, and social media. Late July falls at the height of raspberry season in many regions.
holidays.funFact: A raspberry is not a true berry but an aggregate fruit made of dozens of tiny drupelets, each with its own seed, all clustered around a central core.

holidays.name: World Ranger Day
holidays.description: A day to honor park rangers and wildlife protectors who work to defend nature, often in dangerous conditions. People remember rangers who have been injured or killed in the line of duty and celebrate those who protect wildlife and wild places.
holidays.origin: The International Ranger Federation established World Ranger Day in 2007 on the anniversary of the founding of the organization in 1992. It is now recognized worldwide to raise awareness of the work of conservation rangers.
holidays.funFact: Rangers do much more than guard animals. Their duties can include firefighting, search and rescue, scientific research, education, and even delivering babies in remote areas.

holidays.name: National Avocado Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the creamy green fruit that has taken over toast, salads, and smoothies. Fans celebrate with guacamole, avocado toast, and other avocado-heavy creations.
holidays.origin: National Avocado Day is a modern food holiday popularized through social media and the avocado industry, as the fruit's popularity surged in recent decades. It is celebrated on July 31 in the United States.
holidays.funFact: The word avocado comes from the Aztec word ahuacatl, which also meant testicle, and some historians say the fruit was considered an aphrodisiac.

holidays.name: National Jump in the Puddle Day
holidays.description: A splashy day that encourages people of all ages to lace up their rain boots and jump into puddles for the sheer joy of it. It is a reminder not to take life too seriously and to embrace childlike fun, even on a rainy day.
holidays.origin: This unofficial holiday emerged from the internet's collection of fun days, inspired by the universal childhood delight of puddle jumping. It is often credited to the whimsical spirit of kids' stories and cartoons like Peppa Pig.
holidays.funFact: Peppa Pig made puddle jumping famous worldwide, with her love of 'muddy puddles' appearing in countless episodes and even causing some parents to hide rain boots from toddlers.
